newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus repeats desire for special NATO deal.
newsitem.headline: Belarus repeats desire for special NATO deal.

text.p: Belarus wants a special deal with NATO and the Western alliance should put down in writing its promise not to put nuclear arms on the territory of new members, a senior official in the former Soviet republic said on Friday.

The official was speaking before the end of a U.S.-Russian summit at which the two sides agreed to cut tensions over NATO plans to expand eastwards, which are opposed by Moscow and its small, co-Slav neighbour Belarus.

Viktor Sheiman, secretary of the policy-making Security Council which held a regular session earlier, told a briefing that the expansion of the Western military alliance eastwards directly affected the interests of Belarus.
He repeated an earlier statement by President Alexander Lukashenko that Belarus wanted a special deal on NATO expansion like one being worked on with Russia and Ukraine.
"Belarus declares that we are ready to sign a charter on bilateral relations," Sheiman said.
He said Belarus welcomed NATO's declaration that it would not station nuclear arms on the territory of new members but added: "We must strengthen this with a legal document."

Ural Latypov, Lukashenko's aide on foreign affairs, said Belarus had not changed its critical attitude to NATO expansion, adding: "A list of activities of Belarussian diplomacy in this connection was approved at the Security Council session today."
Lukashenko urged NATO earlier this month to conclude a separate treaty with his country and said a new "European order" should be established without the United States.
Belarus, like Russia, is a member of NATO's Partnership for Peace (PFP) programme but has not taken part in joint military manoeuvres or in officer exchanges with the alliance.
